content: Recent clinical trials have provided robust evidence supporting the efficacy of SGLT2 inhibitors in managing patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD). The DAPA-CKD trial demonstrated that dapagliflozin significantly reduced the risk of worsening kidney function, end-stage kidney disease, and cardiovascular death in patients with CKD, regardless of the presence of diabetes. Similarly, the CREDENCE trial showed that canagliflozin markedly decreased the risk of kidney failure, cardiovascular events, and hospitalization for heart failure in individuals with T2D and CKD. Furthermore, the EMPA-KIDNEY trial confirmed that empagliflozin effectively reduced the progression of kidney disease and cardiovascular complications in patients with CKD, including those with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) as low as 20 mL/min/1.73 m². These findings underscore the critical role of SGLT2 inhibitors in improving renal and cardiovascular outcomes in this high-risk population.
